One non-final rejection was written on 12 June 2018 and mailed 20 June 2018; an applicant-initiated telephonic interview followed on 10 July 2018; the applicant responded on 19 July 2018; and the Notice of Allowability was signed on 13 September 2018. claims.text: THIS IS THE ONE PAIS DEVICE THE NAVY ACTUALLY TESTED, AND THE TEST FAILED. Timothy Boulay, Communications Director at NAWCAD, on the record to Brett Tingley of The War Zone: 'The High Energy Electromagnetic Field Generator testing occurred from October 2016 through September 2019.' 'The cost was $508,000 over the course of three years. Around ninety percent of the total - $462,000 - was for salaries, while the rest was used for equipment, test preparation, testing and assessment.' And: 'When NAWCAD concluded testing in September 2019, the "Pais Effect" could not be proven.' Tier 2 because this is a named official on the record and not a document this board has opened; the underlying FOIA release is not in the board's hands.

desc: The earliest of the five filings and the foundation of the set, since every later device depends on generating and manipulating high-energy electromagnetic fields. Application 14/807943, filed 24 July 2015, granted 20 November 2018, assigned to the Secretary of the Navy. The abstract describes a generator comprising a shell, an electrostatic generator, a power plant and a thermoelectric generator. Its file wrapper was obtained and read on 28 August 2026 and it is the control case for the craft application. One non-final rejection, one telephone interview, one response, and allowance on the ground that the prior art did not show the device. Enablement was never raised. A different examiner in a different art unit handled it, and it too has now lapsed for non-payment of the first maintenance fee.

timeline.label: Application 14/807,943 filed for the Electromagnetic Field Generator
timeline.text: The first of the five Pais filings, assigned to the United States as represented by the Secretary of the Navy. It is the device NAWCAD would later test.

timeline.label: NAWCAD begins testing the High Energy Electromagnetic Field Generator
timeline.text: Timothy Boulay, Communications Director at NAWCAD, on the record: 'The High Energy Electromagnetic Field Generator testing occurred from October 2016 through September 2019.' The $508,000 spent corresponds closely to the two $250,000 lines the PAX 205 invention-disclosure briefing proposed.

timeline.label: The only rejection the electromagnetic field generator ever drew
timeline.text: USPTO mailed the single non-final rejection in application 14/807943. A telephone interview followed on 10 July and the applicant responded on 19 July. Enablement was never raised in this case.

timeline.label: Electromagnetic field generator allowed on prior art, not on enablement
timeline.text: The Notice of Allowability for application 14/807943 allowed claims 1-12 because 'the prior art fails to show' the claimed generator. The craft application, which incorporates this generator by reference, was under appeal at that moment for being impossible.

timeline.label: NAWCAD concludes testing: the Pais Effect could not be proven
timeline.text: Timothy Boulay, Communications Director at NAWCAD: 'When NAWCAD concluded testing in September 2019, the "Pais Effect" could not be proven.' Three years, $508,000, of which $462,000 was salaries. The sponsor tested its own patent and reported the negative result.

timeline.label: The Navy says so publicly, through a named spokesman
timeline.text: Brett Tingley, 'The Navy Finally Speaks Up About Its Bizarre "UFO Patent" Experiments', The War Zone, updated 1 February 2021. This is the citation that replaces the board's previous encyclopedia sourcing for the same fact: a named NAWCAD official quoted by a named reporter, giving the window, the sum, the salary share and the result.

timeline.label: US 10,135,366 expires for non-payment of maintenance fees
timeline.text: The first of the two granted Pais patents lapsed for non-payment of the first maintenance fee, five weeks before the inertial mass reduction patent did the same. USPTO had mailed a maintenance fee reminder on 11 July 2022.
